meta.subject: science
meta.title: The Cell: Unit of Life
meta.summary: What cells are, what their parts do, and how plant and animal cells differ.

chunks.title: Building blocks of life
body: A house is built from bricks. Your body is built from **cells** — tens of trillions of them.
A **cell** is the smallest unit that can carry out all the processes of life. That's why it's called the **structural and functional unit of life**.

chunks.title: Who saw cells first?
chunks.body: In **1665**, Robert Hooke looked at a thin slice of **cork** through his microscope. He saw tiny box-like spaces and called them *cells*, from a Latin word meaning 'small room'.

chunks.title: One cell or many?
body: Most cells are so small that we need a **microscope** to see them.
Some living things are made of just **one cell**, like *Amoeba*, *Paramecium* and bacteria. They are **unicellular**.
Plants, animals and humans are made of many cells. They are **multicellular**.

question.prompt: An *Amoeba* is made of just one cell. So it is…

options.why: *Multi* means many. Humans and mango trees are multicellular; *Amoeba* has only one cell.
*Amoeba* eats, moves, grows and reproduces — all signs of life. Being one cell doesn't make it non-living.
A tissue is a group of many similar cells working together. One cell alone isn't a tissue.

question.explanation: *Uni* means one: a **unicellular** organism is a single cell that does everything to stay alive.

chunks.title: Main parts of a cell
rows: Thin outer layer that controls what goes in and out
Jelly-like fluid where most of the cell's work happens
Controls all the cell's activities; holds the genetic material (DNA)

chunks.title: Plant cells have extras
body: Plant cells have all of the parts above, **plus**:
- **Cell wall** — a stiff layer *outside* the membrane, made of *cellulose*. It gives the plant shape and support.
- **Chloroplasts** — green structures containing *chlorophyll*. They make food by **photosynthesis**.
- A **large central vacuole** that keeps the cell firm. Animal cells have only small vacuoles, or none.

chunks.title: Common trap
chunks.body: Plant cells **do** have a cell membrane. The cell wall sits *outside* the membrane — it's an extra layer, not a replacement.

question.prompt: The green structures in a plant cell that make food are called ___.

mistakes.why: Close! **Chlorophyll** is the green *pigment*. It sits inside the structures called **chloroplasts**.
The nucleus controls the cell, but it doesn't make food.
Mitochondria *release* energy from food. Making food is the chloroplasts' job.

question.explanation: **Chloroplasts** contain chlorophyll and make food by photosynthesis.

chunks.title: Think like a scientist
chunks.problem: A student looks at a cell under a microscope. It has a nucleus, a cell membrane and cytoplasm, but **no cell wall** and **no chloroplasts**. Is it a plant cell or an animal cell?
chunks.hint: Which two parts are found only in plant cells?
steps: List what plant cells have that animal cells don't: a **cell wall** and **chloroplasts**.
It does have the parts that *all* cells share: membrane, cytoplasm and nucleus.
chunks.answer: An **animal cell** — it has no cell wall and no chloroplasts.

flashcards.back: The smallest structural and functional unit of life.

flashcards.front: Who first named cells, and when?
flashcards.back: Robert Hooke, in 1665, while looking at cork.

Made of many cells.
Plants, animals, humans
Controls the cell's activities and holds the DNA.
Thin outer layer that controls what enters and leaves the cell.
Release energy from food — the cell's power station.
Green structure in plant cells that makes food by photosynthesis.
Stiff cellulose layer outside the membrane in plant cells; gives shape and support.

questions.prompt: Which part controls all the activities of a cell?

options.why: Cytoplasm is where much of the work happens, but it doesn't give the orders. The nucleus does.
The membrane controls what enters and leaves, not everything the cell does.
Vacuoles are for storage — water, food and wastes.

questions.explanation: The **nucleus** is the control centre of the cell.

questions.prompt: Which is found in plant cells but **not** in animal cells?

options.why: Both plant and animal cells have a nucleus.
Plant cells need energy too, so both plant and animal cells have mitochondria.
All cells have a membrane. In plants it sits just inside the cell wall.

questions.explanation: The **cell wall** (and chloroplasts) are only in plant cells.

questions.prompt: The scientist who named cells after looking at cork in 1665 was Robert ___.

mistakes.why: Nearly — it's spelled **Hooke**, with an *e* at the end.
Isaac Newton lived at the same time, but cells were named by Robert **Hooke**.

questions.explanation: Robert **Hooke** saw box-like spaces in cork and called them cells.

questions.prompt: Why are mitochondria called the 'power station' of the cell?

options.text: They control what enters the cell

questions.explanation: Mitochondria break down food to **release energy** (respiration).

questions.prompt: A cell from a leaf would most likely have…

options.text: a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole
a cell wall but no nucleus
options.why: Leaf cells do have a nucleus — it controls the cell's activities.
Every cell has a membrane. The wall is outside it, not a replacement.
Plant cells have a large central vacuole that keeps them firm.

questions.explanation: Leaf cells are plant cells, and they're green because they're full of chloroplasts.

questions.prompt: Living things made of only one cell are called ___.
Which of these is a **multicellular** organism?

options.why: *Amoeba* is a single cell — it's unicellular.
A bacterium is a single cell — it's unicellular.

questions.explanation: A mango tree is made of billions of cells working together.
